items.title: Getting robots back on track by reconstituting control in unexpected situations with online learning
items.authors: Maxime Allard, Manon Flageat et al.
items.summary: The researchers tested a system that updates an onboard model rapidly to compensate for unexpected changes affecting a robot. It improved recovery relative to the tested control baselines. The useful question is how adaptation behaves when the original model becomes wrong. The reported gains apply to the experimental disturbances and performance measures, not a guarantee of recovery from arbitrary damage.
items.headline: An online learning controller helps robots recover from disturbances

explainer.finding: An adaptive controller improved robot recovery from tested unexpected changes compared with the study’s control baselines.
explainer.method: The system updated an onboard model during operation and was evaluated under experimental disturbances that made the original model less accurate.
explainer.meaning: A controller may need to revise its expectations when a machine’s behavior changes, rather than keep issuing commands based on an outdated model.
explainer.limits: Recovery from selected disturbances does not guarantee recovery from arbitrary damage. Response time, learning conditions, and failure cases need to stay attached to the result.

items.title: Enhanced sodium storage in hard carbon via solvent co-intercalation electrolyte enabling Ah-level pouch cells at low temperatures
items.authors: Meng Li, Zeping Liu et al.
items.summary: A solvent co-intercalation strategy helps sodium enter hard-carbon electrodes without the usual slow solvent-removal step. The authors report ampere-hour-scale cells with low-temperature performance, including 107 Wh/kg at −50°C on a cell-stack basis excluding packaging. This boundary matters: the result is not a complete battery-pack specification, and commercial cost, safety, and long-term durability require further assessment.
items.headline: An electrolyte design improves sodium-cell performance in extreme cold

explainer.finding: An electrolyte strategy improved sodium-cell operation in extreme cold, with a reported 107 Wh/kg at −50°C on a cell-stack basis.
explainer.method: The authors tested ampere-hour-scale cells using a strategy that lets solvent and sodium enter the hard-carbon electrode together, changing a normally slow step.
explainer.meaning: Ions travel with surrounding solvent molecules. Altering how that layer is handled can help charge move when cold slows the usual process.
explainer.limits: The quoted mass excludes packaging. Whole-pack energy, lifetime, cost, and other operating conditions remain separate questions.

items.title: 60 cm2 perovskite-silicon tandem solar cells with an efficiency of 28.9% by homogeneous passivation
items.authors: Kerem Artuk, Aleksandra Oranskaia et al.
items.summary: The study combines treatments that reduce losses at perovskite surfaces and interfaces, reporting certified efficiency of 28.9% over a 60-square-centimeter active area. Uniformity matters because a method effective on a tiny cell may not scale. This is a device-level result; module production, outdoor lifetime, and total system cost remain separate engineering questions.
items.headline: Surface treatments carry tandem-cell efficiency to a larger active area

explainer.finding: Surface and interface treatments supported 28.9% certified efficiency over a 60-square-centimeter tandem solar-cell active area.
explainer.method: The researchers applied treatments to reduce losses and evaluated the larger perovskite–silicon device, including efficiency certification.
explainer.meaning: A tiny high-performing patch is not enough if defects accumulate across a larger cell. Uniform treatment helps carry useful performance beyond small samples.
explainer.limits: Active-area cell performance differs from module and installed-system performance. Outdoor lifetime, production consistency, and total cost still matter.

items.title: Cementitious Materials
items.authors: National Institute of Standards and Technology
items.summary: NIST describes work on measurement tools and standards for additive construction with cement-based materials. Printing requires a mix that flows through equipment yet supports layers as they accumulate, making timing and material behavior central design variables. This source describes a research programme and demonstrations, not a completed comparative trial or a certification that printed buildings meet every requirement.
items.headline: Printed concrete needs measurements that connect process and strength

explainer.finding: NIST describes a research programme developing measurements for printing with cement-based materials; this is not a newly completed comparison trial.
explainer.method: The programme studies links among material behavior, printing processes, and resulting structures, using research facilities and demonstrations.
explainer.meaning: The mix must flow through the equipment and then support the next layer. Those competing requirements make timing and measurement central to reliable construction.
explainer.limits: A programme description does not certify a building or establish that printed construction outperforms other methods. Specific claims require the resulting technical studies.

items.title: Achieving kilowatt-scale elastocaloric cooling by a multi-cell architecture
items.authors: Guoan Zhou, Lingyun Zhang et al.
items.summary: A prototype combines mechanically compressed nickel–titanium tubes with a heat-transfer fluid and a multi-cell arrangement to achieve kilowatt-scale cooling. The study addresses the challenge of scaling useful heat movement, not only changing a material’s temperature. Actuator work, heat transfer, fatigue, manufacturing, and cost still determine whether such devices can compete in practical applications.
items.headline: A multi-cell design brings solid-state cooling to kilowatt scale

explainer.finding: A multi-cell prototype achieved kilowatt-scale cooling using mechanically stressed nickel–titanium tubes.
explainer.method: The device coordinated tube compression with heat-transfer fluid and multiple cells to move heat through a repeating cycle.
explainer.meaning: A material’s temperature change becomes useful cooling only when a machine repeatedly absorbs heat from one place and releases it elsewhere.
explainer.limits: Actuator work, fluid handling, fatigue, manufacture, and cost affect practical performance. A material effect alone is not a complete refrigerator.

items.title: In-process monitoring and non-destructive evaluation for metal additive manufacturing processes
items.summary: NIST reviews monitoring and non-destructive evaluation for metal additive manufacturing, with particular attention to qualification of nuclear-power components. The report helps distinguish a process signal from evidence about a finished part’s defects and performance. It is a technical assessment of methods and gaps, not proof that any particular printed component is qualified for service.
items.headline: A technical report examines how to qualify printed metal parts

explainer.finding: A technical report assesses methods and gaps in monitoring and inspecting metal parts made by additive manufacturing.
explainer.method: NIST reviews in-process monitoring and non-destructive evaluation, with attention to qualification of nuclear-power components. It is an assessment, not a single qualification trial.
explainer.meaning: A printer’s sensor signal must be connected to something that matters about the finished part, such as a relevant defect. A clean-looking trace alone is insufficient.
explainer.limits: The report does not establish that an arbitrary printed component is fit for service. Material, geometry, process, inspection capability, and application requirements matter.

items.title: Quantifying the impact of cell-to-cell inconsistency on electric vehicle battery degradation and utilization
items.headline: Uneven cell aging can leave usable battery capacity stranded
items.authors: Litao Zhou, Xiaolei Bian et al.
items.summary: Operational data from 116 cars and 17 buses link differences among cells to reduced pack utilization. The estimates depend on calibration and normalization of observational measurements.

evidence.question: How does cell variation constrain a pack?
evidence.limitations: Operational effects cannot be completely separated from intrinsic aging.

explainer.finding: Uneven cells can constrain the complete battery.
explainer.method: The team estimated capacity and resistance from vehicle records.
explainer.meaning: A weak cell can limit what stronger neighbors deliver.
explainer.limits: Model-dependent fleet estimates do not isolate every cause of degradation.

editorialReview.reason: Connects cell variation to pack performance; methods and observational limitations checked.
